Henry IV was a significant figure in the history of Western Europe during the Late Middle Ages, and his reign had a lasting impact on the region. He played a key role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire and was a prominent leader in the region. Henry IV was also a patron of the arts and architecture, and his court was known for its cultural achievements. The legacy of Henry IV can be seen in the continued existence of the Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg, which remains an important part of German history and culture. The impact of his reign can also be seen in the development of the region's trade and commerce, which continued to grow and flourish after his death. The cultural legacy of Henry IV can be seen in the many architectural and artistic achievements of his court, including the construction of the Brunswick Cathedral, which remains one of the most important landmarks in the region. The significance of Henry IV's reign can be understood through the lens of the cultural and political developments of the time, including the rise of humanism and the decline of feudalism.
